  1. General Information

  1.1 Introduction

   Siah Makan Oil field is located 10Km. South of the Bibi Hakimeh and West of the Kilur
   karim Field. SI-1 is about 230 Km. Southeast of Ahwaz and 125 Kms North of the
   coastal city of Bushehr. This field structure is mapped geophysical anticline about 16
   km. long and 10km. wide.

                         Figure 1: Location of Siah Makan Oil Field in the Map

                   Figure 2: Location of Siah Makan Oil field – Side view of Structure

  1.4 Pore and Fracture Pressure Prediction

   As there is no data about pore pressure and Fracture pressure of Siah Makan oil field,
   approximate pore pressure was predicted using Mud Weight history of offset wells in
   each depth with regard to the Loss/Gain and stability situation of the well.

  1.5 Program Outline

     It is planned to drill and complete a Vertical Delineation-Producer well to evaluate and
   produce oil from Bangestan Reservoir of Siah Makan Oil Filed at W030N location.

  W030N will be drilled vertically down to 20 m. TVD in Kazhdumi Formation to total depth
    of 5296.1 m. the well will be completed in Sarvak formation as perforated cased hole
   with 7” * 4 ½” -5K Urban completion.

   26" Hole section:

   26” Hole Section is Drilled 150 m through Aghajari Formation. Aghajari Formation
   Consists of Marl, Sand and Shale. For Drilling This Section Pre-Hydrated Bentonite
  Mud (65-70 pcf) would be used and PHB/HV Sweeps will be used for hole cleaning
   purposes. According to Previous Wells of this Field, this Section is almost Problem Free
   with low risk of Complete to partial loss in surface layers and around rig sub base. Care
   should be given to avoid excessive hole wash out and erosion below the rig sub base.
   The 20’’ Casing will be set at ±150 m and cemented in One Stage using Stinger. 21
  ¼” -2K C.H.H (Weld on Bottom) would be nipple up at this stage and 21 ¼”-2K Annular
  BOP (Diverter) is used for drilling next hole section to divert the potential well flows.

   17 1/2" Hole section:

   17 ½’’ Hole Section is Drilled to 2821.1 m as longest section of the well Through
   Aghajari, Mishan and upper parts of Gachsaran formation. According to Previous Wells
    of this Field, there might be hole problems like bit balling, Tight Hole and Swabbing,
   cave-in and hole wash out which could be due to salt dissolving. The marl & claystone
   can cause low ROP due to bit balling, also can lead to tight hole and swabbing while
    drilling / trip out which may lead to well flowing. 13 3/8’’ and 13 5/8” Casings will be
   set at ± 2821.1 m in Gachsaran formation (10 meter in member No. 6) and will be
   cemented in One Stage (Lead CMT: 98-100 pcf & Tail CMT: 115-118 pcf - Exact CMT
   Program will be Issued in Due Time). PHB/HV Mud would be used for upper parts of
   the interval (Down to about 800 m) and then Salt Polymer Mud (64-98 pcf) would be
   used for deeper parts. CDR/GR log is performed to survey the well path. 21 1/4"-2K *
   13 5/8"-3K C.H.S would be nipple up at this section and 13 5/8"-5K BOP Stack is used
    for drilling next hole section.

   12 1/4" Hole Section:

   12 ¼’’ Hole Section is Drilled through high pressure zones of Gachsaran Formation
   (Mbr#6-1) to 3511.1 m and 9 5/8’’ Casing will be set at ± 3511.1 m, 3 meter in Cap
   Rock and cemented in one stage (Lead & Tail: 139-140 pcf - Exact CMT Program will
   be Issued in Due Time). Salt Saturated Polymer Mud (130-137 pcf) is used for drilling
   the section. According to previous wells, there are risks of well flow from Gachsaran
   high pressure zones, tight holes and swabbing. CDR/GR and SBT logs are performed
    to evaluate the well path and cement quality behind the 9 5/8’’ casing, respectively. 13
   5/8"-3K * 11''-5K T.H.S and 13 5/8’’- 5K BOP Stack are nipple up at the end of the hole
    for drilling next hole section.

   8 3/8” Hole Section:

   This Section will be drilled vertically in Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam and 2 m of Sarvak
   formations to 4621.1 m. 7’’ liner will be set at 2990- 4621.1 m in sarvak formation and
   cemented in one stage (S.W: 116-118 pcf- Exact CMT Program will be Issued in Due
   Time). For drilling this section, Salt/ KCl/ Glycol/ Polymer mud (70-95 pcf) will be
   used. Based on Offset Wells History, Drilling Risks of this interval are Tight Hole and
   Stuck Pipe, H2S Exposure, Well Flow coupled with Mud Losses, High sensitivity to Swab
   and Flow. Complete loss also has been observed in Pabdeh, and Heavy losses in Upper
   Gurpi. Also, there  is risk of gas flow in Ilam and High-pressure flow in Pabdeh
   Formations. CDR/GR and SBT (inside 7’’ LNR) logs would be performed as per
   program.

   5 7/8’’ Hole Section:

   This Section will be drilled vertically in Sarvak and Kazhdumi formations down to 20 m
  TVD in Kazhdumi formation to Well TD 5296.1 m. 5’’ liner will be set at 4561.1-5296.1
  m and cemented in one stage (S.W: 116 -118 pcf- Exact CMT Program will be Issued
    in Due Time). Salt/ KCl/ Glycol/ Polymer mud (70-90 pcf) will be used for drilling the
    section. CDR/GR, Fullset, Image, RFT and SBT (inside 5’’ LNR) logs would be
   performed as per program. Coring will be done from Zones No. 4,5 and 6 of Sarvak
   Formation. According to offset wells data, there are risks of Tight Holes, Stuck Pipe,
   H2S Exposure and Well Flow in this section.

   Perforation and Completion:

   Based on completion scenario of this well, after cementing 5’’ Liner, the well will be will
   be perforated and completed (by 7” *4 ½” –5K Urban completion String) in Sarvak
   formation (around 100 m perforation interval, based on Reservoir evaluation logs). In

  2. Geological Information

  2.1 Formation Description

  A brief description of the stratigraphic units expected to be drilled in W030N location
   has been presented in the following breakdown.

      Aghajari Formation

         This huge clastic/marly formation (2232.6 m thickness) with Pliocene-Pleistocene
           in age  is mostly composed of red marls, interbedded sandstone and red
         claystone beds. It is expected that the red claystone intervals increase from top
           to the bottom of the formation. The sandstone and siltstone layers are variably
          consolidated and generally can be described with light brown and light gray
           colors, fine to medium sand grains, well sorted and sometimes are dominated by
         sub-angular to sub-rounded quartz grains. The above-mentioned sandstones are
         loose (un-consolidated), friable to moderately hard.

        The marls are red, reddish brown to pale reddish brown, generally sticky and
            slightly silty, soft to firm, grading to claystone. The clay stones are red color,
        sometimes show dark brown, generally soft, sticky and amorphous, locally some
          calcareous, grading to gray marl, generally non-silty and occasionally mottled.

         26” (and 17 1/2”) hole sizes would penetrate into the Aghajari formation and then
         20” casing shoe will be set at the near top of this formation, approximately in the
         depth of 150 m (MD).

     Mishan Formation

        The Mishan formation (about 449 m thickness) with Middle Miocene in age is
         mainly comprised of alternated marls and limestone beds in this well, overlying
          the topmost Gachsaran anhydrite layer. 17 1/2” Hole size will be penetrated
          within this marly/ carbonate formation.

     Gachsaran Formation

        The Gachsaran formation (about 838 m thickness) with Early to Middle Pliocene
           in age, is predominantly made up of evaporates (anhydrite) beds, which are
         interbedded with gray to red marls. In terms of drilling hazards, the Gachsaran
          formation can be subdivided into two (2) main intervals, called Upper and Lower
         Gachsaran.

        The Upper Gachsaran, which corresponds to members 2 to 7, is predominantly
       made up of an alternation between anhydrite and grey marly beds. The marly

                                                                                  Page 29 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                 Drilling Program For
                                  Well: W030N
                           Siah Makan Oil Field

Page 30 of 208              Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05                 Rev:05

         succession is gray to light gray color and soft, which is observed as interbedded
          with some anhydrite beds. The relevant anhydrite is white, milky, soft, partly
           crystalline and medium hard to hard. The red marls are present and show variety
           of colors, ranged from red brown to brown, characterized by soft and sticky
           lithology. 13 3/8” casing shoe will be set at near top of Gachsaran formation, 10
     m in member no. 6, in depth of 2821.1 m (MD). Otherwise, 12 ¼” hole size will
        be penetrated into the most body of Gachsaran formation.

        The Lower Gachsaran unit usually corresponds to member 1 or named Cap Rock
            unit, including alternated salt and anhydrite beds (in form of hard and crystalline
          rocks).   It  is  noteworthy  that  the  basal  part  of Gachsaran  formation  is
          characterized by dark grey to grey marls, accompanied with thin salt beds and
         interbedded anhydrite layers. It is expected that the 9 5/8” casing shoe will be set
           at the basal part of Gachsaran formation, 3 meter in member no. 1, at depth of
         3511.1 m (MD).

     Asmari Formation

        The top of the Asmari formation (430 m Thickness) with Oligocene-Miocene in
         age, is marked by limestone which is white to tan, fine grained, anhydritic and oil
          stained. At the top of the middle Asmari Formation is a sandstone Which is
        medium-coarse grained sucrosic, dolomitic and  oil stained. Anhydrite and
          anhydritic limestone are also present and below, dolomite and  dolomitic
         limestone are present and interbedded with grey to red-brown shaly marl Locally
           staining. It is planned that the hole size 8 3/8” will be penetrated into this clastic/
         carbonate formation.

     Pabdeh Formation

        The top of the Pabdeh Formation (351 m Thickness) with Paleocene-Eocene in
         age, is identified by marl and shale which is calcareous and sandy and by
          increasingly argillaceous limestone, some of which is detrital and sandy, from
           lithological point of view, much of Pabdeh Formation consist of marly limestone,
          Archie, types I and II that is gradational with marly shale which is locally very dark
         grey to black. It is planned that the hole size 8 3/8” will be penetrated into this
          marly/ carbonate formation.

      Gurpi Formation

        The top  of the Gurpi Formation (216 m Thickness)  with Campanian  to
          Maastrichtian in age is gradational from argillaceous limestone to calcareous

                                                                                  Page 30 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                 Drilling Program For
                                  Well: W030N
                           Siah Makan Oil Field

Page 31 of 208              Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05                 Rev:05

          shale. much of the Gurpi Formation consists of shale, medium to light gray
         grading to shaly limestone.  It  is planned that the hole size 8 3/8”  will be
         penetrated into this marly/ carbonate formation.

      Ilam Formation

         This formation (94 m Thickness) is mostly consisting of limestone interbedded
          with shale and claystone beds. The limestone is cream, buff to buff gray, light
         brown, soft to medium hard, chalky, type  II, A,  oil stained, partly  slightly
          argillaceous. The shale is green gray to light green gray, mostly brown gray,
       medium hard, pyritic and slightly calcareous. The claystone is green gray to light
         green gray, soft and slightly calcareous.

                It is planned that the hole size 8 3/8” and 5 7/8’’ will be penetrated into this marly/
         carbonate formation and 7’’ liner shoe will be set at top of sarvak Formation at
         4621.1 m.

      Sarvak Formation

         This formation (657 m thickness) with Albian/Cenomanian-Turonian in age is
         mainly  characterized by  bioclastic carbonate  successions, which  indicate
          reservoir quality. mostly consisting of off white, cream, buff to cream and white
           to cream, soft, soft to medium hard, chalky limestone interbedded with claystone,
          argillaceous limestone, shale, argillaceous dolomite and dolomitic limestone
         beds. The claystone is gray, soft, sticky and high calcareous. The argillaceous
         limestone  is white gray to  light gray,  light  buff, medium hard and  slightly
          bituminous. The shale  is dark brown, dark gray, black, medium hard and
          calcareous. The argillaceous dolomite is buff gray and hard. The dolomitic
         limestone is buff gray to light brown gray and hard. The dolomitic limestone is
          grey, partly light gray and medium hard. It is planned that the hole size 5 7/8” will
        be mostly penetrated into this huge carbonate formation and cased using 5’’
           Liner.

     Kazhdumi Formation

        The lithology of the Kazhdumi Formation consists of shale and shaly limestone.
             5’’ liner shoe will be set 20 m TVD in Kazhdumi Formation at 5296.1 m (Well TD).

3.2 Offset Wells Mud Weight Study

Due to Unavailability of Pore Pressure and Fracture Pressure Data of Siah Makan oil field, it is of
vital importance to study offset wells mud weight history and the effects of mud weight on well
stability, wall caving, tight holes and loss/gain situations in each drilled interval. Following is graphical
illustration of used Mud weights in wells SI-005 and SI-004 with Detailed study of Mud Weight
behaviors.

3.2.1 Well SI-005 Mud Weight Graph

Following diagram depicts the Mud Weight history of well SI-005 and the latter table summarizes
mud weight changes’ details along with some additional data about hole problems, taken actions and
etc.

3.3 Drilling Risks & Pit falls

  ❖ Care should be given to avoid Rig sub base wash out by adjusting Mud Flow Rate and ROP.
      Complete loss may happen in first Hole section meanwhile drilling as happened in some
        offset wells. care should be given to be ready for curing the losses.

  ❖  Aghajari and Mishan Formations’ lithologies consist of soft, sticky Marl and Clay. Care should
      be given to avoid Bit Balling by adjusting Hole Cleaning Hydraulics and Mud Properties.
       Since, there is a risk of Bit Balling, Overpull and Drag Force should be well monitored
        specially during trips to avoid excess Swab forces caused by balled up BHA.

  ❖ While drilling in massive salt formation of Gachsaran Formation, be careful of well trajectory
      and the salt’s cave-in/dissolving.

  ❖ Formation Fluid from Asmari, Pabdeh and Sarvak formations containing harmful hydrogen
        sulfide (H2S) has the risks to harm site personnel during the operation. The H2S content in
      Sarvak Formation is 5600 ppm according to the information provided by the company. All site
       personnel should pay more attention on H2S hazards, and all H2S equipment should be in
      good condition.

  ❖ According to the information provided by company in scope of work, there is no valid
       information about H2S content of Asmari and Pabdeh Formations. But it is supposed that
       both formations contain hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and H2S equipment are considered to be in
       service before drilling the reservoir sections.

  ❖  Lost circulation may occur in upper parts of Pabdeh formation as complete loss happened in
       SI-005 at (@ 3680 m W/88 pcf mud wight). Also, High Pressure Flow has been considered
        for Pabdeh formation as a Potential Well Control Challenge. Heavy, Partial and Seepage mud
       losses are predicted for other formations.

  ❖ As seen in nearby wells, Reservoir sections are highly sensitive to swabbing. It should be
       avoided to make a trip out without wipering tight holes or removing the balling up.

  ❖  Asmari and Sarvak Formations are prone to get the string stuck.

4. Sequence of Operation1

4.1 26” Hole Section

4.1.1 General

 Casing Point                 20” Casing @ 150 m

 Formation                    Aghajari Formation
                            Rig Subbase Wash out / Erosion, Partial to Complete Mud
 Risks & Hole problems
                              Loss, Almost Problem Free
 Deviation Control        TOTCO

 Logging                  N/A

                        PRE-HYDRATE BENTONITE MUD - HV SWEEPS

                MW (pcf)                     65 - 70

                                  Vis. (sec/qt)                   >70

                     PV (cp)                                      -
 Drilling Fluid Parameters
                     YP (lb/100ft²)                 > 30

                         10 Sec / 10 Min Gel (lb/100ft²)        -

                          API FL (ml/ 30min)           NC

                    PH                               9.5 - 10.5

                   GPM                          850-1000

 Drilling Parameters      WOB (KLBs)                    20-45

                   RPM                          80-120

4.1.2 Sequence of Operation
     1.   Check Pre-Spud Check List, P/U BHA & Stand back DPs. Prepare Drilling mud.
     2.   P/U 26’’ R.Bit(bit#1) and Make up 26” BHA as per BHA design. Tag formation at ±14m.
     3.     Drill ahead formation down to 150 m (20” casing point in Aghajari formation) using Hi-
           Vis bentonite Sweeping pill, periodically. Pay enough attention to drill straight hole.

1 Note: Detailed procedure of each operation for all sections, will be issued and sent to rig in due time before performing the operation.

                                                                                   Page 54 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                             Drilling Program For
                              Well: W030N
                        Siah Makan Oil Field

 Page 55 of 208        Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05           Rev:05

     Note:

        -  The exact TD will be determined based on casing tally.
        -  Run Inclinometer to evaluate the verticality of the hole.
        -  Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable
          condition.
        -  Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.
        -  Enough Mud Material, LCM and Cement Should be Available before spudding the
            rig to use if necessary.
        -  Mud Logging unit should be available from rig spud.

4.    Circulate and Clean the Hole, Sweep the Hole Prior to Casing Running  till Shaker
     Clean.
5.   Perform Condition Trip Prior to Run Casing.
6.   Run Survey (TOTCO) to Check Inclination.
7.   Spot hi-vis pill. POOH and L/D Bit and BHA.

     Note:

        -   At TD, Circulate and Clean the hole. Take Survey, POOH to surface. Check the
            Bit.
        -   Perform a Condition  trip due to conditioning the hole prior to run casing.  If
        observed any indication of drag, run back to bottom. Wash and ream to make
         sure that the hole condition is good.

     Preparation / Off-Line Operation:

        -  Ensure 20” casings and accessories are ordered/ready prior to start drilling 26’’
          hole.
        -   Prepare 20” casings, Clean and Drift them, install centralizers.
        -  Make up and thread lock float shoe to the first 20” casing joint and Stab-in float
           collar below the second joint (It should be made in the work shop).
        -   Whilst drilling 26” hole, prepare for nipple upping BOP’s.
        -   Whilst pulling out of hole with 26’’ BHA, pick up 20” casing running equipment.

8.   Perform Pre-Job Safety Meeting (PJSM).
9.   Rig Up Casing Running Equipment.
10.  Run ±150m (Approx. 15 Jts) 20", 106.5 ppf, K-55, BTC Casing with stab-in type shoe
      to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe should be adjusted to have enough
      stick up (1 m on rig floor). Fill casing by non-LCM fresh mud.
11.  RIH W/ Stinger and 5" DP's, Sting-in and Check, Secure Drill Pipe, Circulate and
     Check Stinger for sealing.
12.  Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth
       will be done in due time. Displace Cement with mud (1-2 bbls Short Displace). Monitor
      pressures. Record and Report the final pressure, Sting out. Check the float. POOH
     one stand, circulate to flush/clean drill pipe.

                                                                             Page 55 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                             Drilling Program For
                              Well: W030N
                        Siah Makan Oil Field

 Page 56 of 208        Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05           Rev:05

13. POOH to surface. L/D Stinger While W.O.C to Get Hard, perform top Job If Needed.

     Note:

        -  Take care when running casing not to set down excessive weight if tight hole or
         ledges are encountered.
        -  Shoe and float valves should be inspected and checked before making up.
          Visually inspect shoe joint for debris.
        -  Ensure the tally is followed (Make a note of centralizers used and on what joint).
        Any changes or rejects to be noted and WSS to be informed immediately.
        -  Do not jerk the string at any time.
        -  Mud loggers to prepare swab /surge calculations. Running speeds shall be
          controlled to ensure surge pressures are not excessive. Mud loggers to monitor
        and advise driller.
        -  Secure the Casing on rig floor to prevent sudden upward jumping/movement.
        -  Check the return through the stinger. Check for returns through the casing/stinger
         annulus when circulating conventionally through the stinger.
        -  Run stinger on DP’s using the “C” Plate and 5” x 20” centralizer. Sting in. M/U &
           test cementing lines. Circulate for one casing annulus volume. While circulating,
        check the DPs annulus for any return. Use all DPs weight on the string if observing
        any minor leakage through DPs annulus.
        -  Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected
         depth will be done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbls Short Displace).
         Monitor for pressures. Record and report the final pressure, Sting out. Check the
            float. POOH one stand, Circulate to flush/clean drill pipe.
        -   After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor & flush it.
        -  Keep the casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check for
         casing to be center inside conductor pipe.

14.  Rough Cut Conductor Pipe and 20" Casing, Dress & Bevel Casing Neck suitable to
       install and weld casing head housing, install 21 1/4"-2K C.H.H (Slip on Welded
     Bottom), Weld & Test the sealing of welded casing. (Limit pressure to a maximum of
    80% of the collapse strength of the casing). Outlets must be aligning with cellar stairs.
15.  N/U 21 1/4"-2K Annular BOP (or Diverter) and related lines and valves and test all.
    N/U Bell Nipple & Flow line.
16.  P/U 17 1/2'' R.Bit and Next BHA, Stand Back DP and DC's as Needed for next Hole
      Section.
17.  RIH W/ D/O BHA (Junk Sub Included) and 17 1/2" R. Bit, Drill Out Shoe track and
     cement below shoe. Monitor and Report Drill Out Parameters. Pump periodic pill while
       drilling shoe track. Watch carefully for any indication of abnormal torque, since there
     might be a possibility of shoe being backed off. Report any problem immediately. Drill
     shoe track with low drilling parameters. Record Drill out parameters (Duration/ROP/Bit
      Dull Condition) of Shoe/Collar and Report to Office.

                            Siah Makan Oil Field

          Note:

                -  Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to perform
               top-up jobs.
                -     If there is no cement return to surface, a top job should be performed to fill the
               annulus. Use same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry. Ensure the
                  availability of adequate X-over for connecting line pipe to cement line. The cement
              should be accelerated with max. (2%) Calcium Chloride BWOC and no other
                additives. Wait for the top job cement to get hard.
                -   Pre heat Casing Head Housing before welding.
                -  Check the wear bushing, Plug Tester and 20” * 13 3/8” OD Casing Slip and seal
             assembly in C.H.H before installing C.H.H (on Surface).
                -  The height of spacer spool must be designed where the outlet of spool placed
             above the ground level.

          IMPORTANT NOTE:
                -    If cellar is standard the distance between its top flange and ground level
            must be 1.73 m.
                -    If cellar is not standard the base of C.H.H should not be more than 10 cm
            upper than the floor of cellar.
                -  The rig should be made center again, before starting the next hole operation.

     18.   Fill up the following forms and send to drilling office:

                -   26’’ Bit Report / Record
                -  20” Casing Tally
                -  20” Casing Running Report
                -  20” CSG Cement Report
                -  26” Hole section Summary
                -  Wellhead Diagram with Dimension Serial Number

4.2.3 17-1/2” Section Potential Drilling Challenges

Loss of Circulation / Mud Loss:

    ▪  Maintain MW as plan MW.
    ▪   Control running speed to prevent surge effect.
    ▪   Control mud rheology.

Stuck of Drill String:

    ▪   Closely monitor losses while drilling.
    ▪  Maintain MW as plan MW.
    ▪  Minimize the overbalance (by decreasing mud weight)
    ▪  Minimize stationary time of drill string.
    ▪  Optimize fluid properties in attempts to minimize the risk of sticking.

Casing Stuck Due to Hole Cleaning, Hole Geometry, Loss/Flow or Tight Hole:

    ▪  Avoid creating ledges by easing bit in harder formation and reaming transition between
       formations.
    ▪  Watch casing string weight, understand and monitor casing drag up and down.
    ▪  Avoid thick mud cake by controlling fluid loss and solids.
    ▪   Circulate hole clean prior to POOH for casing.

Bit Balling:

    ▪   Entire bit and/or stabilizers, teeth balling and bottom balling can be reduced by having a
        sufficiently inhibitive mud.
    ▪   Entire bit Balling risk will be reduced by consistently high flow rates, and good hole
       cleaning.
    ▪  Ensure of pumping at high flow rates to produce sufficient HSI.
    ▪  Avoid excessive WOB while drilling through Mishan/Gachsaran formations.

   Actions once balling has been detected:
    ▪   Bits can be cleared if balling is detected early enough and proper actions are taken.
    ▪  Reduce WOB when ROP drops, pick up bit off bottom as quickly as possible and
       increase flow rate.
    ▪  Spin bit off bottom with high RPM and high flow rate for a period of time.
    ▪  Resume drilling with low weight on Bit.
    ▪  Prepare to pump Balled Up Remover pills, leave to soak and try to dissolve/loosen
       balled material.

4.3.3 12 1/4” Section Potential Drilling Challenges

Salt water flow / Swabbing

    ▪  Gachsaran formation has the potential of salt water flow. The hardness of this water is
      between 35000 - 53000 mg/l, so any increase in the hardness of mud would be an
        indication of possible salt water flow. Therefore, during drilling this section, hardness of
       the system must be checked and monitored regularly for any increase in Ca++ ions.
    ▪  Gachsaran formation consisting mainly of Anhydrite and Marls with inter beds of salt.
    ▪  Ghachsaran formation also consists of marly limestone. This is a potential salt-water flow
       zone.
    ▪  Maintain MW as planned MW. Avoid excessive WOB while drilling through Gachsaran
       formation.
    ▪  Check Calcium ions (Ca++) while drilling, in case of showing increasing trend, drilling to be
       stopped. Observe the well and take Proper Action / Mud treatment.
    ▪   Closely Monitor to avoid bit balling which may cause swabbing and well flow during trip
       outs from tight sections of the hole. Try to POOH while pumping out.
    ▪  Flow check if fast break experienced.
    ▪   In case of flow show, increase MW Step Wise. Circulate at least a bottom’s up prior to
     POOH.
    ▪   Special care must be taken when the BHA is inside the previous casing. In contrary to
       popular belief, pressure does travel easily in drilling fluids, so tripping speed must be
        controlled to avoid swabbing.
    ▪  Do not forget to take Slow Pump each 6 hours (200, 300, 400 Psi SPP).

Tight Hole:

    ▪  There is a severe risk of tight hole and pipe stuck in this section. Meanwhile Drilling, work
       out tight hole and tight spots by performing on time Wiper/Condition Trips.
    ▪   In case of facing frequent tight holes not removed by wiper trips, it should be informed to
      head office to decide the mitigation scenario. It may need to Adjust MW, Work on Mud
       rheology, Change BHA or perform additional wiper trips.

Bit Balling:

    ▪   Entire bit and/or stabilizers, teeth balling and bottom balling can be reduced by having a
        sufficiently inhibitive mud.
    ▪   Entire bit Balling risk will be reduced by consistently high flow rates, and good hole
       cleaning.

────────────────────────────────────────────
                                   Drilling Program For
                                   Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

       Page 68 of 208        Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05           Rev:05

    ▪  Ensure of pumping at high flow rates to produce sufficient HSI.
    ▪  Avoid excessive WOB while drilling through Gachsaran formations.

   Actions once balling has been detected:
    ▪   Bits can be cleared if balling is detected early enough and proper actions are taken.
    ▪  Reduce WOB when ROP drops, pick up bit off bottom as quickly as possible and increase

4.4.3 8-3/8” Section Potential Drilling Challenges

Well Control

    ▪  Before entering Pabdeh formation, make sure to have proper Mud weight.
    ▪  Rig well control equipment (BOP stack) and all of PVT sensors shall be function tested
        prior to commence drilling 8 3/8" section.
    ▪  The Rig key personnel (Tool pusher, Driller, Assistant Driller, Derrick man, Shaker man)
        shall be well trained to take prompt action in case of well control situation.
    ▪  Good communication between involved parties is a most.
    ▪   Trip sheet and pit levels (Active / Trip tank) shall be recorded and monitored at all time.
    ▪   In case of swabbing, the plan is trying to bullhead the swab (If it is possible to inject into
       formation) rather than bring the swabbed influx to surface.
    ▪  Take SCR as per procedure and when needed.
    ▪  Stop drilling if any severe losses.

Drills

   Perform Following Drills while inside 9 ⅝" Casing:
    ▪  H2S drill
    ▪  Well control drill
    ▪  Pump over the burners

Sour Gas (H2S)
    ▪  Sour gas has been Reported to be present in reservoir sections of Siah Makan Oil Field.
    ▪  Breathing Apparatuses shall be monitored and serviced in scheduled manner and ensure
       ready to be used efficiently and safely. All rig personnel must be trained properly.
    ▪  The drilling fluid shall be treated to have proper pH and H2S scavenger shall be added
       precautionary to combat any possible sour gas.
    ▪   Sufficient amount of H2S scavengers shall be kept on board.

────────────────────────────────────────────
                                   Drilling Program For
                                   Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

       Page 73 of 208        Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05           Rev:05

    ▪  The corrosion inhibitor will be sprayed on drilling string while tripping out of hole.

Tight Hole and Pipe Stuck:

    ▪  There is a severe risk of tight hole and pipe stuck in this section. Meanwhile Drilling, work
       out tight hole and tight spots by performing on time Wiper/Condition Trips.
    ▪   In case of facing frequent tight holes not removed by wiper trips, it should be informed to
      head office to decide the mitigation scenario. It may need to Adjust MW, Work on Mud
       rheology / Additives or perform additional wiper trips.

Well Flow coupled with mud losses:

    ▪  As observed in nearby wells of SI-004 and SI-005, in this section there is a possibility well
       flow in which increasing the MW will turn the well situation to mud losses. In case, be
       ready to cure losses using reservoir friendly LCM pills.

6.2 26” Hole Section

 26" Hole Size                             20" Casing Size

 From: Surface                            To: 150 m

              150 meters to drill in Aghajari Formation Using PHB /HV Mud

6.2.1 Interval Discussion

Aghajari:     Mainly Limestone inter bed upward with Marl and Gypsum

26" hole will be drilled down to the 150m in Aghajari formation. The 20’’ casing shall cover this
troublesome hole section, where formation instability is the most probable problem. Drilling Fluid
of this section is a simple Spud Mud as below formulation of Pre-Hydrated Bentonite Mud at
minimum 60-70 sec/qt Marsh Funnel Viscosity.

Frequent sweep of the hole by thick PHB HV Pills (FV≥120 sec/qt.) provide adequate hole
cleaning and wellbore stability. Sweeping the hole by 30 bbl HV pills for every 10 m drilled is a
good practice, though the best decision is made according to observation of the actual situation.
Volume of the sweeping pill is subject to be increased prior to make pipe connections.

When section TD is reached, hole should be swept with a large volume of thick Hi-Vis pill to
ensure the hole is quite clean, then a batch of PHB Hi-Vis is spotted in full volume of the open
hole considering the probable hole wash out.

6.2.3 Fluids Formulation:

Pre-Hydrated Bentonite
To prepare a volume of Pre-Hydrated Bentonite, flush the engaged lines and pits, then fill-up 80%
of the pit with drill water. Make sure the chloride content of the base water is less than 600 mg/lit.
Maintain Total Hardness at range of below 200 mg/lit and pH at 10-10.5 by adding Soda Ash and
Caustic Soda. Add Bentonite at rate of 15-20 lb/bbl and keep the centrifugal mixing pump working
and leave the pit for at least 3-4 hours to let the Bentonite well hydrated.

6.2.4 Mixing Procedure

Drill water with chloride less than 600 mg/L would be used to prepare Bentonite mud:
    1.   Fill the pit with calculated amount of Drill Water.

    2. Add proper amount of Soda Ash to treat out hardness below 200 mg/lit.

    3. Add proper amount of Caustic Soda to have a constant pH of 10 in the pit.

    4. Add 15-20 lb/bbl of Bentonite and let to hydrate and agitate for at least 4 hours to reach
to the maximum yield.

High Viscous Sweep Pill

           FLUID PROPERTIES                FORMULATION

          Property         Range        Product      Concentration (lb/bbl)

     Mud Weight (pcf)      65 - 70
                                                                Drill Water             0.965
      Funnel Vis (sec/qt)       > 70
                                               Bentonite           25 - 30
      YP (lb/100 ft²)        > 25
                                            Caustic Soda   Depends on Base Water
          pH             9.5 – 10.5
                                      Soda Ash    Depends on Base Water
           FL           NC

Drill Water must be checked prior to mixing Bentonite to be sure about the Salinity. If salinity
of base Drill Water is high (more than 1500 mg/L), mixing Bentonite mud and pill will not be
effective and viscosifier polymers must be added to aid the Hi-Vis pill forms otherwise another
source of Drill Water should be supplied.

High Viscous Pill by Polymer:
    1- Take a batch of weakly-yielded Bentonite mud/pill in the pit.

    2-  Maintain its hardness below 200 mg/lit and its pH is at range 9.5-10.5

    3- Add gradually Xanthan Gum or CMC-HV or Natural Gum to reach desired viscosity.

 6.3 17-1/2” Hole Section

  17 1/2" Hole Size                        13 3/8" Casing Size

  From: 150 m                              To: 2821.1 m

     2671 meter to drill in Aghajari, Mishan, Gachsaran formations using PHB/HV and Salt
                                    Polymer mud

6.3.1 Interval Discussion

 Aghajari, Mishan, Gachsaran:     Mainly Limestone inter bed upward with Marl and Gypsum

 Formations to drill:

        Aghajari: Marl, Sandstone, Limestone
       Mishan: Marl, Sandstone, Limestone
      Gachsaran (Member#7): Marl, Anhydrite

 This section is planned to be drilled from 150m to ±800m generally by using Bentonite mud while
 hole is cleaned by pumping PHB or Hi Viscous polymer pills. Volume of the mud remained from
 previous section can be used here for making batches of Hi-Vis pill. After ±800 m, drilling is
 resumed by changing the mud system and displacing the hole with fresh Salt/ Polymer Mud. This
 mud system lets us drill through Aghajari, Mishan and Gachsaran (member#7 only) formations
 down to section TD at 2821.1 m where the shoe of 13 ⅜" casing will be set in Anhydrite layers of
 top of member#6 of Gachsaran formation.
 Xanthan Gum at the range of ≥1 ppb provides hole cleaning characteristics of the active fluid.
 Starch NF at 4-5 ppb will be used to control the API Fluid Loss in desired range around ±10.
 Centrifuges and Hydro cyclones should be run while drilling this section to keep Low Gravity Solid
 content less than 7% and therefore minimize reactive solids.
 In case of having Bit Balling, spot 30-50 bbl pill of Salt Saturated Caustic Soda Chrome-Free
 Lignosulphonate around BHA and soak for 10 minutes with high RPM. Pipe RPM at range of 120-
 150 is recommended otherwise limitation of the bit or another BHA component dictates less.
 When TD is reached, a minimum circulation of one and half times of hole volume should be
 performed prior to make the wiper trip to surface.

6.3.3 Properties Discussion

Mud Weight

  Mud weight is planned for this section to be at range of 64-98 pcf. Controlling of MW could be
  done by running all SCE while dressing the shakers with finest possible mesh screens and
  dumping mud from sand trap and dilution instead.

Plastic Viscosity
   Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control
   equipment, coupled with new mud dilution.

API Fluid Loss Control
    It is recommended that the API fluid loss be maintained ±10 ml/30min after displacing the hole
   Salt Polymer Mud. This may best be achieved by the addition of a combination of Starch NF at
  4-5 ppb.
   * Note: It should be noted that for the last 500 meters of 17 ½’’ hole section, API FL will be
   controlled to be less than ±5 ml/30min. PHPA (as cutting encapsulator) and KCL (as clay
  swelling inhibitor) are Considered as Optional Chemicals to be used in case of need.

Rheology
   Maintain the Yield point in the range of 15-25 lb/100ft² to ensure having adequate hole
   cleaning, making adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. Thixotropic characteristic of
   the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized rheological profile with
   elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning characteristics which result in fluid
   with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Total Hardness
   Total hardness should be maintained below 1000 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance with
   the addition of Soda Ash and Caustic Soda.

pH and Alkalinity
  pH should be maintained in the range of 9-10 using Caustic Soda. This will maximize chemicals
  performance and minimize corrosion problems.

6.3.4 Solids Control Management

   Shakers to be dressed initially with proper mesh screens. There may be a requirement to
       dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize
       loss of mud over shakers.

   Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear
       motion shale shaker with hydro cyclone and centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuges
       should be run at high flow rate on LGS mode to remove low gravity solids and keep mud
       weight and properties in range.

   Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment.
         All efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 7%. Ensure full utilization of primary
        solids control equipment while drilling, however dump and dilution would be inevitable.

6.3.7 Mixing Procedure

    1.   Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.8 bbl/bbl

    2.  Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash for desired range of pH and Ca²⁺ content

    3.  Mix Starch NF at 4 ppb and PAC LV at 1 ppb at the rate of 1 sack per 7 min

    4.  Mix Xanthan Gum at 1 ppb and PHPA at 0.3 ppb at the rate of 1 sack per 15 min
    ➢  Wellsite mud engineer may know it better to add PHPA in circulating system drilling
         and not in initial mixing

    5.  Mix KCl 10 ppb (this step will be optional, in Case of need below depth of 2000 m, KCL
         will be added to control clay swelling and dispersion)

    6.  Mix Salt 80 ppb or more based on the MW required for the displacing mud, while
       considering 10 ppb KCl,

    7.  Adjust mud weight to desired figure as per hole condition by Barite
    ➢  Instead of Barite, CaCO3 can be used as weighting agent as well as Bridging Agent in
             Filter Cake
    ➢  While having minimum 20 ppb CaCO3 in system, further weight up of the
         system can be by adding Barite in order to have less solid content

     In case of foaming use Alcohol-Base Defoamer

6.3.8 Drilling Issues

Stuck Pipe

  Mud must be inhibited to avoid the reaction with the Clay-based lithology to be drilled. In case
   of stuck pipe, Environment-Friendly Non-Weighted Pipe-Freeing pill can be spotted around the
  stuck area while working on pipe according to instruction of operation department.

Lubricity

   In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 0.5-1.5% by volume. This
   lubricant should be of the type of Water-Dispersible Readily Biodegradable which causes
   minimal environmental impact and provides characteristic of string wet-ability by reduction of
   surface tension. This results in less chance of bit and BHA balling and enhances the ROP.

Downhole Losses

   Concentration of LCM will vary according to the size of losses. In the event of seepage losses,
  no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate over the time and drilled
  depth shall be made. In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare pills at
   different grades and concentrations, and spot it over thief zone. The concentration may vary
  between 20 to 100 ppb.

  Below procedure  is supposed to be followed  in case that various rates of losses are
  encountered in the course of drilling, though the most effective plan is the one which is
  customized based on actual situation on site:

      Losses less than 10 bbl/hr.:
        ➢  No action to be taken, but close monitoring of the loss shall be made
      Losses 10 - 30 bbl/hr.:
        ➢  Load Kwik-Seal F in system up to 10 ppb

                   If no success, then:
        ➢  Pump 50 bbl. LCM pill containing:
                  ▪  3-6 ppb Mica Medium
                  ▪  7-12 ppb Walnut Shells Fine
                  ▪  7-12 ppb Kwik-Seal Fine & Medium
                  ▪  3-6 ppb CaCO3-M
             Note: System is loaded gradually from low concentration to maximum mentioned
                     ranges.
      Losses 30 – 100 bbl/hr.:
        ➢  Load CaCO3 Medium & Coarse in active system up to 5 ppb of each

LCM Pill Application Procedure

     1.  After spotting LCM pill over thief zone, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait
       30 minutes and monitor the annulus. After 30 minutes, attempt to  fill the annulus,  if not
        already full.
     2.   If the hole can be filled, close the BOP and squeeze 10 bbl of LCM pill into the formation
        without exceeding 200 psi.
     3.   If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
     4.   If the LCM pill failed to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot
        another 50 bbl of LCM pill.
     5.  Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill into
        the formation without exceeding 200 psi.
     6.   If a squeeze pressure develops, hold pressure for 1 hour before running the string to
        bottom.

    All LCM pills must be thoroughly mixed and homogenized and enough viscous before
       pumping.

6.4 12-1/4” Hole Section

 12 1/4" Hole Size                        9 5/8" Casing Size

 From: 2821.1 m                           To: 3511.1 m

    690 meters to drill in Gachsaran (#2-6) and Cap Rock formations using Salt Saturated
                                   Polymer mud

6.4.1 Interval Discussion
Gachsaran (Members #6 to #1): Marl, Salt, Limestone, Arg. Limestone, Anhydrite

This section will be drilled from 2821.1 m to 3511.1 m as section TD through Gachsaran formation
from member#6 to member#1 where the shoe of 9 5/8’’ casing will be set in member#1 namely
Cap Rock. This section is designed to drill high pressure layers of Gachsaran formation separately
from low pressure lower interval.

Fluid system here is somehow similar to what used in previous section. The most salient
difference is the mud density which is planned to be increased up to 137 pcf to eliminate the risk
of Salt Water Flow, which is the well-known characteristic of high pressure Gachsaran members.

Depends on the specification of the drilling rig in terms of tanks capacities and solid control
efficiency, mud volume left on board from the previous section can be carried over to this section,
treated for desired properties, loaded with additional products and weighted up to desired mud
weight.

This is important to note that, using the mud of the previous section is a cost-effective practice
though need to build new volumes of fresh dilution and fresh mud is a must and for sure inevitable,
especially, if Solid Control Equipment of the rig are not that efficient to discard LGS effectively.

The base fluid for the mud is the Drill Water in which 109 ppb of NaCl Salt is solved. This gives a
Salt Saturated brine of density 75 pcf. Of course, no CaCO3-F is going to be used here, but Barite
is the primary weight agent which is used alone until mud weight 120 pcf and for higher mud
densities it is recommended to use also Hematite with the ratio of 1:2 against usage of Barite.
This aids in having lower solid content in the system.

Since having a thin filter cake, as a result of tight fluid loss, is a safety factor against the probable
risk of mechanical stuck pipe, and in the other side, the tight fluid loss itself is a potential aid for
being far from occurrence of differential stuck pipe, Starch NF at 10 ppb is formulated as fluid loss
controllers in this mud system.

Because of the high density and high solid content of the mud of this section, slip velocity of
cutting particles is easily lower than the annular velocity at routine flow rate of drilling the section,
therefore, there would be no need to add any viscosifier such as Xanthan Gum as hole cleaning

accurate idea of what the fact actually is.

When TD is reached, a minimum circulation of two times of hole volume should be performed
prior to make the wiper trip to surface. Monitoring the shakers for being clear of cutting helps in
deciding when to stop circulation.

6.4.3 Properties Discussion

Mud Weight

  Mud weigh has been planned for this section to be at range of 130 to 137 pcf. Controlling of
 MW could be done by running SCE and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens and
  dumping mud from sand trap and dilution instead. As it was mentioned earlier, the base fluid
   for the mud here, i.e. Drill Water in which 109 ppb of NaCl Salt is solved provides a Salt
   Saturated brine of density 75 pcf. Adding Barite until mud weight 120 pcf and for higher mud
   densities adding both Barite and Hematite at 2:1 ratio is the solution to achieve desired mud
   weight.

Rheology
   Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an
   optimized rheological profile with elevated low-shear rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning
   characteristics which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity. Plastic
   viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment,
  coupled with new mud dilution.

                                                                                  Page 101 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                   Drilling Program For
                                   Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

API Fluid Loss Control
    It is recommended that the API fluid loss be maintained <2 ml/30min after displacing the hole
   with Salt Saturated Polymer Mud. This may best be achieved by the addition of a combination
   of Starch NF at 10 ppb.

MBT

  Measuring of MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT of range of below 10 is
   acceptable here. Using fine screens and high-speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower
   values of MBT by discarding the fine solids and consequently minimizes the dilution rate.

Total Hardness
    Total hardness should be maintained below 1200 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance
    with the addition of Soda Ash and Caustic Soda.

pH and Alkalinity

   High density water-based fluids are usually more sensitive to changes in pH value in terms of
    stability in parameters, especially rheology and gel strength. An experienced safe range of pH
     is between ±9.5, though on-site mud engineer shall distinguish the best figures by means of
    pilot testing and monitoring the active system.

6.4.4 Solids Control Management

    Shakers to be dressed initially with proper mesh screens. There may be a requirement
          to dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to
        minimize loss of mud over shakers.

    Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment.
           All efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 7%. Ensure full utilization of
         primary solids control equipment while drilling, however dump and dilution would be
          inevitable. It is the best if the rig is equipped with an efficient Barite Recovery System.

6.4.5 Interval Key Issues

     Drill the cement inside the casing with a batch of lowest quality of mud received
        from previous section and one or two meters before 13 3/8” casing shoe, pump 30
         bbls of Hi-Vis pill prior as a sweep.

    Use pre-mixes to maintain system volumes and making necessary dilutions.

    Ensure to have sufficient volume of Kill Mud with needful density on hand.

     Properties of the Kill Mud should be as close as possible to the active system, but
          at a density of minimum 15 pcf (optimum 20-30 pcf) more and for a volume of

6.4.8 Mixing Procedure

      1.   Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.62 bbl/bbl

      2.  Treat water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash for desired range of pH and hardness

      3.  Mix Starch NF at 10 ppb at the rate of 1 sack per 7 min

      4.  Mix Salt 109 ppb

      5.  Adjust mud weight to desired density (up to 120 pcf) by adding Barite
     ➢  For MW above 120 pcf  it is recommended to use also Hematite with the
               ratio of 1:2 against usage of Barite
       In case of foaming use Alcohol-Base Defoamer

6.4.9 Drilling Issues

Salt Water Flow

  While drilling this section care should be done for salt water flow and the key factor is controlling
  the mud weight and good hole monitoring. Mud properties  for increment  of Chloride
  concentration and Calcium ion concentration must be checked carefully for any changes.

  Detecting the slight to moderate increase in chloride content is usually not very easy because
  the system itself is saturated of this ion. But drop of MW-out and increase of TH and Ca²+ are
  much more visible and informing in this regard. These parameters shall be monitored several
  times in each mud engineer shift and in case of observing any unexpected jump, MW must be
  increased quickly.

  Having sufficient stock of weight agents and also kill mud is a must. Also, any unexpected drop
   of pH can be a sign of probable flow, because formation water generally has low pH value.
  Constant monitoring of drilling parameters for any unexpected improve of ROP, drop of SPP
  and drop of drilling torque must be considered as hints to be in the risk of flow or kick. Having
  an eye on mud logging Flow Paddle for any increase is another point of attention.

Stuck Pipe

  Mud must be inhibited to avoid the reaction with the Clay-based lithology to be drilled. In case
   of stuck pipe, Environment-Friendly Non-Weighted Pipe-Freeing pill can be spotted around the
  stuck area while working on pipe.

Lubricity

   In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 0.5-1.5% by volume. This
   lubricant should be of the type of Water-Dispersible Readily Biodegradable which provides the
   characteristics of string wet-ability by reduction of surface tension. This results in less chance

Downhole Losses

  The concentration of LCM will vary according to the size of losses. In the event of seepage
   losses, no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate over the time and
   drilled depth shall be made.

   In the event of moderate to high rate of downhole loss, prepare pills at different graded

  Ensure that the LCM pill is displaced out of the string prior to shutting down the mud pumps.

  Below plan is to be followed prior to intersecting the known/expected loss zones while drilling
   notorious formations and in case losses are encountered:

            ▪  5 ppb CaCO3-C

    ➢  Spot 60-90 bbl pill containing:

           ▪  10 lb/bbl Kwik-Seal F

6.5 8-3/8” Hole Section

 8 3/8" Hole Size                           7" Liner (2990- 4621.1 m)

 From: 3511.1 m                           To: 4621.1 m

   1024 meters to drill in Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi and 10 m of Ilam formations using Salt/ KCl/
                                      Glycol/ Polymer Mud

6.5.1 Interval Discussion

Formation to drill

    •  Asmari: Limestone, Sandstone, Dolomite, Marl
    •  Pabdeh: Shale, Marl, Limestone, Arg. Limestone
    •   Gurpi: Limestone, Marl, Arg. Limestone
    •   Ilam: Shale, Limestone

8 ⅜” Interval will be drilled through formations of Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi and Ilam formations. Salt/
KCl/ Glycol Polymer Mud is designed for drilling this section. Shoe of 7" liner will be set at 4353.1
m, 10 m in Ilam Formation. Different rates of downhole losses, from seepage to complete, may
be experienced through this section. Tight hole leading to pipe stuck is the other risk of drilling
here.

Based on the lithology to be drilled in 8 ⅜” hole section, it is necessary to utilize shale inhibitors
in active system. The primary shale inhibitor in the system is Potassium ion for cation exchange
in the clays structure, to reduce their capacity of hydration and swelling. This will be provided by
KCl concentration of ≥18 ppb, but to be added only 100 m prior to reach Pabdeh formation (due
to probable losses in Asmari formation). KCl will be allowed to be depleted gradually in the course
of drilling. It will be maintained only if situation dictates.

NaCl (45 ppb) should be solved in base water to get 72 pcf brine. Starch NF at 4-5 ppb and PAC
LV at 1.5-2 ppb will be used to control the HPHT Fluid Loss below 9 ml/30min and keep the filter
cake as thin as possible on bore hole. 1-1.5 ppb Xanthan Gum provides both suspension capacity
for adding CaCO3-F as weight agent to reach desired MW and required cutting carrying capacity
to clean the hole. Use of Barite should be avoided as it can damage Ilam and Sarvak reservoirs.

Glycol, as shale inhibitor is going to be mixed at 7-10 ppb equivalent of 2-3% by volume 100 m
before we reach the top of Pabdeh formation. It should be a Medium-Cloud Point Glycol with the
primary function of shale inhibition for water-based muds. It can be used while drilling Pabdeh
shales without further maintaining to let it be depleted from the system gradually.

In order to retard degradation of natural-source polymers, using sorts of polymer extender such
as Oxygen Scavenger S and pH Buffer Agent is helpful.

6.5.7 Mixing Procedure

1.   Fill tanks with calculated amount of Seawater 0.9 bbl/bbl

2.  Treat Drill water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash

3.  Mix 5-6 ppb Starch NF and 1.5-2 ppb PAC LV at rate of 1 sack per 7 min

4.  Xanthan Gum at range of 1 ppb at rate of 1 sack per 15 min

5.  Mix NaCl at 40 ppb

6.  Adjust mud weight as per hole condition by adding CaCO3-Fine

Note: As it was mentioned in section 6.5 Discussion above, KCl, Glycol and Sulfonated Asphalt
      are not planned to be mixed in initial preparation of mud. They are supposed to be added
       in the system as per below plan:

   ➢ KCl
      To be added 100 m prior to reach Pabdeh formation due to probable losses of
        Asmari. It will be mixed at initial concentration of 18 ppb, but is supposed to be
        maintained in range 18-25 ppb to section TD, unless hole condition dictates
        otherwise.
   ➢ Glycol
      To be added while drilling through Pabdeh formation and Laffan formation. In each
         of these formations,  it will be mixed at initial concentration of 2-3% by volume
        without further maintaining to let  it be depleted gradually, unless hole condition
         dictates otherwise.
   ➢ Sulfonated Asphalt
      To be added while drilling through Laffan formation while drilling through Pabdeh
        formation and Laffan formation. It will be mixed at initial concentration of 3-5 ppb
        without further maintaining to let  it be depleted gradually, unless hole condition
         dictates otherwise.

6.5.8 Properties Discussion

Mud Weight

  Mud weigh has been planned for this section to be at range of 70-95 pcf. Controlling of MW
   could be done by running hydro-cyclones and centrifuges and dressing the shakers with finest
  mesh screens and dumping mud from sand trap and dilution instead.

Plastic Viscosity
   Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control
  equipment, coupled with whole new mud dilution.

Fluid Loss
    It is recommended that HPHT Fluid Loss be maintained below 9 ml/30min during the section.
  This is be achieved by the addition of a combination of Starch NF at 5-6 ppb and PAC LV at 2
  ppb.

Rheology
   Maintain the Yield Point in the range of 15 to 22 lb/100ft² to ensure having adequate hole
   cleaning, making adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. Thixotropic characteristic of
   the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized rheological profile with
   elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning characteristics which result in fluid
   with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Total Hardness
    Total hardness should be maintained below 800 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance with
    the addition of Soda Ash and Caustic Soda.

pH and Alkalinity
  pH should be maintained in the range of 9 to 10 using Caustic Soda. This will maximize
  chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems. Note that using pH Buffer Agent (as
  Polymer Temperature Stabilizer) results in developing an increase in pH value. As the product
   provides buffering characteristic over the pH, obviously, this pH is very stable.

MBT

  Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT of range of below 10
   is acceptable. Using fine screens and high-speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower
  values of MBT by discarding the fine solids and consequently minimizes the dilution rate.

Shale and Clay Inhibition

  Shale and Clay inhibition will be achieved by utilizing KCl at range of 18-25 lb/bbl and Glycol
   at range of 2-3% by volume.

6.5.9 Drilling Issues

Stuck Pipe
  Evidences of tight hole and stuck pipe occurred in some wells while drilling this Section. Mud
  must be inhibited to avoid the reaction with the shale and proper mud weight must be controlled.
   In case of stuck pipe, Environment-Friendly Non-Weighted Pipe-Freeing pill can be spotted
  around the stuck area while working on pipe.

Hole Cleaning

  Xanthan Gum is the base for Rheology in the KCl Polymer system. If additional Rheology is
   required, increase Xanthan Gum concentration to enhance hole cleaning. Xanthan Gum will be
  used to provide an optimized rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high
  shear-thinning characteristics which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Carbon Dioxide

   Although  it is unlikely to detect Carbon Dioxide in this section, based on an established
   protocol, the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically CO2.
   In case of Carbon Dioxide contamination, Lime should be added at 0.5-2 ppb in order to
  remove CO2 in the form of precipitating Calcium Carbonate.

Hydrogen Sulphide

  Regardless that the interval has or has not the potential of emitting any gas, this is an
   established protocol that the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here
   specifically H2S. If any trace of H2S is detected, treat the mud with 1-2 ppb Zinc Carbonate and
   increase pH by Caustic Soda to maintain it around 10. Corrosion Inhibitor should be used in
   this case at range of minimum 1% by volume.

Lubricity

   In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 1-2% by volume. This
   lubricant should be of the type of Water-Dispersible Readily Biodegradable which provides the
   characteristics string wet-ability by reduction of surface tension. This results in less chance of
    bit and BHA balling and enhances ROP.

Downhole Losses

   Concentration of LCM will vary according to the size of losses. In the event of seepage losses,
  no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate over the time and drilled
  depth shall be made. In the event of moderate to high rate of downhole loss, prepare pills at
   different graded concentrations and spot over thief zone. The concentration may vary between
  25-35 lb/bbl. Ensure that LCM pill is displaced out of the string prior to shutting down the mud
  pumps.

formations and in case losses are encountered:

    Losses less than 10 bbl/hr:

     ➢ No action to be taken, but close monitoring of the loss shall be made
    Losses 10 - 30 bbl/hr:

     ➢  Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 5-7 ppb
     ➢  Load CaCO3-C in active system up to 5-7 ppb

            ▪  5 ppb Kwik-Seal Fine
            ▪  5 ppb CaCO3-M

                  ranges.

     ➢  Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 7 ppb
     ➢  Load CaCO3-C in active system up to 7 ppb
     ➢  Load Kwik-Seal F in system up to 5 ppb
   Shaker-man should be ready for managing a part of the return flow toward the pit-
      room by-pass shakers to avoid screens get blinded and LCM get wasted.

        we need to pump the pill through a Mule-Shoe while following the procedure of the
           next state.

     In the event of severe losses, Squeeze Pills, Barite or CaCO3 or Cement Plugs, Silicate

 LCM Pill Application Procedure

    1.  After spotting LCM pill over thief zone, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait
      30 minutes and monitor the annulus. After 30 minutes, attempt to  fill the annulus,  if not
       already full.
    2.   If the hole can be filled, close the BOP and squeeze 10 bbl of LCM pill into the formation
       without exceeding 200 psi.
    3.   If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
    4.   If the LCM pill failed to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot
       another 50 bbl of LCM pill.
    5.  Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill into
       the formation without exceeding 200 psi.
    6.   If a squeeze pressure develops, hold pressure for 1 hour before running the string back to
       bottom.

   Notes:

     All LCM pills must be thoroughly mixed and homogenized and enough viscous
        before pumping.
    Remove filter screens from the drill pipe and if necessary, remove the strainers
       from the mud pumps suction lines.

 management plan for dealing with returns from running and cementing casing, with contingencies
 or lost circulation and dealing with spacer returns and contaminated mud. Reduce YP to minimum
 level (if practical) prior to cement job.

6.6 5-7/8” Hole Section

 5-7/8" Hole Size                            5" Liner (4561.1 – 5296.1 m)

 From: 4621.1 m                            To: 5296.1 m (TD)

        761 meters to drill in Ilam, Sarvak formations using Salt Saturated Polymer mud

6.6.1 Interval Discussion

Sarvak: The lithology of the Sarvak Formation is consisting of limestones, locally dolomitic and
interbedded with marly limestone and bituminous shale.

This section will be drilled at mud weight 70 to 90 pcf and Salt Saturated/ KCl/ Glycol/ Polymer Mud
system will be used. The possible risks of this section are downhole losses, flow of gas and/or oil
and tight hole which may lead to stuck pipe. Severe losses were experienced in porous layers.
Starch HT at 5-6 ppb and PAC LV at 1.5-2 ppb will be used to control the HPHT Fluid Loss below 9
ml/30min and keep the filter cake as thin as possible. Differential Stuck pipes can be encountered in
this section therefore it is vital to keep thin filter cake.
Polymer Temperature Stabilizer (PTS) which is a pH-Buffer agent and polymer extender for water
base drilling fluid is formulated to be utilized in active system at range of ±0.25 ppb, equivalent of
0.075% by volume. This product helps in having longer life time of the polymers when bottom hole
static temperature exceeds 250 ºF (120 ºC). In general, we can say that such a pH-Buffer agent
extends thermal resistivity of many common polymers, reduces polymers consumption as their
degradation is retarded, and reacts with and neutralizes acid gases, a common problem in high
temperature wells.
To minimize the risk of polymer fermentation whilst drilling, Oxygen Scavenger S is formulated at
concentration of 0.3 ppb while having routine daily treatment as well. A very commonly used type of
oxygen scavenger is a Sodium Sulphate-based product.  It reacts with and eliminates dissolved
oxygen as a factor of increasing fermentation rate of natural-sourced polymers and also as a potential
source of metal corrosion in mud systems.
Xanthan Gum is used as the base of a thixotropic Rheology to provide adequate YP and high LSRV
(Low Shear Rate Viscosity) and high-shear-thinning-viscosity which are the key factors to ensure
adequate hole cleaning.

6.6.4 Properties Discussion

Mud Weight

   Density of base water will be increased by combination of Salt (85 ppb) and KCl (15 ppb) to get
   brine at density of 75 pcf, then for increasing the density up to 79 pcf, combination of CaCO3-F.

Rheology
   Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized
   rheological profile with elevated low-shear rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning characteristics
  which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity. Plastic viscosity should be
   maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new
  mud dilution.

Water-Dispersible Lubricant

    It should be an environmentally friendly, biodegradable and non-damaging lubricant which
   increases the lubricity of the system and reduces the torque and drag, compatible with most water-
  based muds. It is formulated at range of 1-2% by volume in this interval.

Oxygen Scavenger

  Oxygen Scavenger S should be added directly in the active pit and not through mixing hopper,
   otherwise it will mostly scavenge the oxygen of the air and not the oxygen trapped and/or solved
   in the mud. Besides the initial treatment of the system with 0.25 ppb of this product, daily treatment
   of maximum 0.1 ppb is recommended.

Clay-based Lithology Inhibition; a matter of caring reservoir as well

   Inhibition of hydratable lithology is going to be provided by addition of 5%-wt. KCl and minimum
  2% by volume of High Temperature Cloud Point Glycol. Potassium Chloride  is used as a
   Clay/Shale Inhibitor where clay can be existing in limestone layered. The concentration required
    will be based on the extent of the clay but will generally vary from 3-5% by weight in the system.
  Use of KCl in reservoir mud has also the good effect of minimizing the hydration and consequently
   swelling of the clay-based lithology of the pore’s walls. This helps in less damage to the reservoir
  caused by inevitable mud invasion.

   In the opposite side, since KCl of the mud is a disturbing factor for the quality of the Gamma log,
     it is offered to have initial sufficient concentration of KCl (along with formulated 2-3% Glycol) in
   the system to commence a safe and smooth drilling through Kazhdumi formation, but let the KCl
   to be depleted and not maintained in the course of onward drilling, so that the concentration of
   disturbing potassium ion drops down. Glycol is going to play the role of primary shale inhibitor for
   the intervals exposed to low-KCl mud.

pH-Buffer Agent & Polymer Extender

  pH buffer and polymer extender  for water base  drilling  fluids  is used when bottom-hole
   temperatures range from 250 ⁰F to 350 ⁰F. In this section downhole temperature will reach to 275
   ⁰F so this polymer extender will be used at 0.25 ppb, equivalent of 0.075% by volume to retard
  polymer degradation. Note that addition of this product into the system must be gradually in
   several stages of very small batches, because it can cause a sudden jump in pH value if used in
   large batches.

Bio-Cide

   Starch HT, PAC LV and Xanthan Gum are subject to bacterial degradation even in saturated
   brines; therefore, a biocide should be used in the system to retard this happening and extend lift-
   time of the said products.

6.6.5 Solids Control Management

   Shakers to be dressed initially with proper mesh screens. There may be a requirement to
       dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize
       surface loss of mud.
   Combination of linear motion shale shakers with centrifuges proved best results. If centrifuges
       are planned to run in Barite Recovery mode (to discard  drill solids but keep MW and
       properties in range), it should be noted that there is the risk discarding CaCO3. Running retort
        test on samples of centrifuged fluids gives ideas on how justifiable the plan is.
   Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All
        efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 7%.

6.6.6 Interval Key Issues

   Mud weight in this interval is critical for wellbore stability and successful drilling and hole
       condition will dictate the mud density
    Cuttings should be circulated up above the BHA prior to connections.  It should also be
       considered to ream at each connection. This will minimize the potential of cuttings settling
       during connections, causing packing off and stuck pipe. Prior to trips the hole should be
        circulated for at least 1.5 times of annular volume circulation should be done prior to make a
       wiper trip to surface. Monitoring the shakers for being clear of cutting helps in deciding when
        to stop circulation. This will prevent tight hole on the way out and bridges, fill etc. on the way
      back in.
    Maintain a contingency stock of Caustic Soda, Zinc Carbonate, Lime, Citric Acid, Barite and
        fine and medium size of acid-soluble LCM on board.
    Total Hardness content in the filtrate should be controlled less than 600 mg/lit by using Soda
      Ash and Caustic Soda for better performance of polymers.

 6.6.9 Mixing Procedure

     1.   Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.81 bbl/bbl

     2.  Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash

     3.  Mix 5-6 ppb Starch HT, 1.5-2 ppb PAC LV at rate of 1 sack per 7 min

     4.  Mix KCl at 15 ppb and NaCl at 94 ppb

     5.  Addition of pH-Buffer, Oxygen Scavenger S, Corrosion Inhibitor, ZnCO3, Bio-Cide and Glycol
          is while drilling as required

     6. Add CaCO3-F (45 ppb) to reach MW of 79 pcf

      In case of foaming use Alcohol-Based Defoamer

      In case of excessive torque use Lubricant at range of 1-2% by volume.

6.6.10 Properties Discussion

 Rheology

    Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized
    rheological profile with elevated low-shear rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning characteristics
   which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity. Plastic viscosity should be
   maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new
   mud dilution.

 Fluid Loss

     It is recommended that the HPHT Fluid Loss be maintained at <9 ml/30min. This may best be
   achieved by the addition of 6 ppb Starch HT and 3 ppb PAC LV. Offering other High-Temp Drill-In
   Fluid Loss controllers is welcome and usage is subject to be investigated.

 Total Hardness

   Total hardness should be maintained below 600 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance with the
   addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda.

 pH and Alkalinity
   pH should be maintained in the range of 9 to 10.5 using Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda. This will
   maximize chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems.
