6.6.11 Drilling issues

 Stuck Pipe

   The main actions to take in order to avoid differential sticking are tight fluid loss control, and
   continuous movement of pipe and controlling mud weight. In the event of stuck pipe, environment-
    friendly pipe-freeing pill can be spotted around the stuck area. The other candidate in this case
   can be using HCl 10-15%. Because of undesired side effect damage to metallic parts and hole
   wash out, using acid is only considered for highly dramatic situations.

 Hole Cleaning

   The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning, are VG-meter 6 and 3 dial readings. A rule of
   thumb is to have the low shear-rate values approximately the same as the hole size for deviated
   holes and it can be considered slightly less for a vertical well. Prior to connections, the cuttings
   should be circulated well above the bottom hole assembly to avoid packing off after connections.
   Hole should be circulated clean before starting to POOH or back reaming.

   Parameters affecting Hole Cleaning:
     1.  Monitoring shakers to become clear of cutting is a key factor to judge if the hole is clean.
     2. Pump as fast as possible.
     3.  Control ROP's must be considered to avoid heavy load of cuttings in annulus.
     4.  In laminar flow the hole cleaning capacity, especially at low shear rates in large diameter
        sections, can be improved by raising the low shear-rate viscosity & gels. The best indicators
           will be the 6 & 3 rpm and initial gel.
     5.  Another point to consider is measuring the relaxing time. Relaxation measurements are made
         after the standard viscosity determinations have been compiled with the viscometer. After
       you have determined the last viscosity (3 rpm dial reading), shut the viscometer off and
       measure the time it takes for the dial to fall back to zero. Fluids which exhibit an extended
        relaxation time indicate improved hole cleaning and suspension characteristics.

 Lubricity

    In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 1-2% by volume. This lubricant
   should be of the type of environment-friendly water-dispersible readily biodegradable which
    provides the characteristics of string wet-ability by reduction of surface tension. This results in less
   chance of bit and BHA balling and enhances ROP.

 Hydrogen Sulphide

   Regardless that the interval has or has not the potential of emitting any gas, this is an established
    protocol that the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically H2S.
      If any trace of H2S is detected, treat the mud with 1-2 ppb Zinc Carbonate and increase pH by

                                                                                   Page 125 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                    Drilling Program For
                                    Well: W030N
                             Siah Makan Oil Field

        Page 126 of 208        Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05           Rev:05

   Caustic Soda to maintain it around 10. Corrosion Inhibitor should be used in this case at range of
  minimum 1% by volume.

Carbon Dioxide

   Although it is unlikely to detect Carbon Dioxide in this section, based on an established protocol,
   the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically CO2. In case of
  Carbon Dioxide contamination, Lime should be added at 0.5-2 ppb in order to remove CO2 in the
  form of precipitating Calcium Carbonate.

Downhole Losses

   Losses/Differential sticking  will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized
  bridging/weight material (and Polymer)  in conjunction with appropriate  drilling practices.  If
  seepage losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the
   loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 microns is
  recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.

  CaCO3 will minimize filtrate/whole mud invasion of the reservoir and reduce potential problems of
  losses and differential sticking. The fluid loss and cake quality are two of the most important mud
   properties to prevent or alleviate potential stuck pipe. Note that, the maintenance of the correct
  amount and size of bridging material cannot be over-stressed.

       Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr.

       No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

        Losses from 10-30 bbl/hr.
      ➢ Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb
      ➢ Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, add 100 kg per 5
            meters drilled to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

              High concentrated LCM  pill of various sizes of Calcium Carbonate should be
            pumped and spotted and gently squeezed over the loss zone.

    Spotting Procedure
     1.  After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes
       and monitor the annulus.
     2.  After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled,
        close BOP and squeeze 10 bbl LCM pill into formation without exceeding 200 psi.
     3.   If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
     4.  Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and
        spot another 50 bbl of LCM pill.
     5.  Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill
         into the formation without exceeding 200 psi.
     6.   If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before running the drill
         string back to bottom.

    Notes:
     LCM pills must be thoroughly homogenized and viscous enough before being
          pumped.
     Pumping high-concentrated LCM pill is subject to use of open-end DP or Mule-Shoe.
         Use of PBL Sub is a good practice too.
     Remove filter screens from the drill pipe (if there is any) and if necessary, remove
             strainers from the mud pump suction lines.

6.6.12 Logging, Casing Running & Cementing

 It is most importance that the hole is clean prior to logging and running liner. Any adjustments to mud
 properties, such as reduction of gel strength, before logging and before running liner  will be
 discussed. Make pit management plan for dealing with returns from running and cementing casing,
 with contingencies or lost circulation and dealing with spacer returns and contaminated mud. Reduce
 yield point to minimum level (if practical) prior to cement job.

   6.7 Completion Fluid

          Clear, solids-free brines are the most commonly used fluids in completion and
      work over operations to minimize formation damage whilst perforation job and
      completion phase to improve production rate.

      Completion and work over fluids are specialized fluids used during well completion
      operations and remedial work over procedures. These fluids must control not only
      subsurface pressure with density, but also must minimize formation damage during
      completion and work over operations.

     The use of fluids that cause minimal formation damage can result in dramatically
      improved production. Most reservoirs are sensitive to any fluids other than those
      contained in them naturally.

        All surface pits need to be cleaned and flush all lines, then prepare inhibited sea
      water to displace hole to be ready for completion the well.

      pH: Corrosion is accelerated in acidic environments (pH <7) and retarded in alkaline
       conditions (pH >7). As the pH (pH = -log [H+]) is increased, the concentration of H+
         will be reduced, which may slow the corrosion rate. Conversely, decreasing the pH
      increases the concentration of H+ ions, which increases the cathodic reaction and
     may increase the corrosion rate (acids tend to dissolve metals faster).

      Normally, a pH of 9.5 to 10.5 is adequate to mitigate most corrosion. In some cases,
     a pH as high as 12 may be required. High pH values (>10.5) neutralize acid gases
     and lower the solubility of corrosion products.

   Corrosion:

          Salt  solutions are  often  highly  corrosive.  Dissolved oxygen and massive
      concentration of ions are the primary corrosive agents in sodium-, potassium-,
       calcium-chloride- or bromide-brine base completion fluids. The solubility of oxygen
        in these brines decreases as saturation with the  salt  is approached. Anyhow
       corrosion inhibitor at concentration of 1% by volume and oxygen scavenger (special
      type compatible with Calcium brines) at concentration of 0.2 ppb should be added in
      completion fluid to minimize the risk of corrosion.

        Appearance of some corrosion inhibitors available in market is amber in color and
        slightly dark (not 100% clear). Using these types of product may cause reading the
        turbidity somehow more than what recorded before adding  it. Selecting a type of
       corrosion   inhibitor  that  besides  providing  the  expected  metal  protection
       characteristics causes excess value of NTU as less as possible is a point which
     needs to be considered.

                                                                                Page 130 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                  Drilling Program For
                                  Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

Page 131 of 208              Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05                 Rev:05

    Alkalinity:

         Corrosion is accelerated in acidic environments (pH<7) and retarded in alkaline
       conditions (pH >7). As the pH (= -log [H+]) is increased, the concentration of H⁺ will
     be reduced, which may slow the corrosion rate. Conversely, decreasing the pH
      increases the concentration of H⁺ ion, which increases the cathodic reaction and may
      increase the corrosion rate (acids tend to dissolve metals faster).

         Normally, pH of 9 to 10 is adequate to mitigate most corrosions. In some cases,
      higher pH may be required. High pH values (≥9) neutralize acid gases and lower the
        solubility of corrosion products. This value of alkalinity is achieved in Calcium brines
      by adding 1-2 ppb Lime.

   Dissolved Oxygen:

          In order to eliminate the threat of dissolved oxygen as a possible source of
       corrosion, use  of Oxygen Scavenger CA  is formulated  in completion  fluid at
      concentration of 0.2 ppb. Oxygen Scavenger CA is a catalyzed Sodium-based
      chemical used to scavenge oxygen dissolved in Calcium Brines and also drilling
        fluids having more than 300 ppm filtrate Calcium. It lowers the risk of corrosion and
      extends the life of metallic parts including production tubing. It is a stable solid and
      does not deteriorate when exposed to the atmosphere for extended periods of time.

       Oxygen Scavengers must be added directly through the hatch from the top of
       suction pit, not using/running mixing pump and just prior to pump the fluid into the
        well. Although, the concentration is very little, since this stage is after filtering the
       brine,  it is recommended to do a pilot test in lab to ensure turbidity remains in
      acceptable range after adding this material.

   H2S Scavenger:

       Use of liquid H2S scavenger, as a preventive safety factor, is recommended to be
     added at concentration of 0.1 ppb in completion fluid.  It should be of the type
      designed specifically for brine-base fluid systems to remove H2S.

   6.7.1 Filtration

     Due to sensitivity of the completion assembly and packer components and the
    importance of proper packer setting, it is of high attention to set the packer in a solid-
    free environment. For this purpose, filtering packer fluid and completion fluid is a
    solution. Filtration units are, generally, of two types; using Bag Filter or Cartridge Filter.
    Cartridges separate finer solid particles than what bag filters do. The most commonly
   used bags are 50μ, 25μ and 10μ, and routine cartridges are 10μ, 5μ and 2μ. The best

                                                                                Page 131 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                  Drilling Program For
                                  Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

Page 132 of 208              Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05                 Rev:05

     is to have both types of filtration units and sufficient stuck of bags and cartridges. In
    order to speed up the rate of filtration, on both bag unit and cartridge unit, it is highly
   recommended to employ Dual Chamber units. They not only can handle more flow rate,
    but also, lead the flow more evenly with lower invasion rate over the filter elements (bag
    or cartridge) which results in their longer lifetime.

       After the brine is prepared, it should be left for minimum 12 hours to let maximum
    possible number of solid particles settled, then as explained earlier, the fluid should be
    transferred to another clean pit by means of an air-powered Wilden pump without
    sucking the dirty residue at the bottom of the pit. This brine should again be left for few
    hours to have the chance of optimum settling. Now,  it should be filtered first through
   bag filters and then through the cartridge filters. Conductance of the filter elements (bag
    or cartridge) depends on the specs of the packer assembly. However, the finer filtering,
    the safer packer setting.

     TSS (Total Suspended Solids) and Turbidity (NTU: Nephelometric Turbidity Units) of
   a fluid are the parameters that are used to express the extent to which the fluid is free
    of solids. These factors are measured on wellsite using a HACH® Test Kit. Most of the
    operations, require TSS and NTU ranging 30-50. Here, we need TSS<30 and NTU<40
    for the fluid pumping in the well and both TSS and NTU less than 100 for the returned
     fluid. These figures are best achieved if 10μ bag filters and 2μ cartridge filters are used.

    10.  Perforation Program

           it is planned to perforate the well in Sarvak Formation (5’’ Liner- Around 100 m- Based on
      Reservoir log evaluation) using 2 7/8” HSD gun with 60 degrees Phasing and 6 SPF density.
      Perforation interval will be determined after logs evaluation. Due to Completion Scenario of the
      well and Possibility of Well Plug Back to 400 m above TD and perforating the new upper
       Interval, Exact Perforation program will be issued in due time.

      At any time during perforating, if unsure or the information is questionable, then do not continue
      with the perforating operations. Seek assistance and  clarification. Once the casing  is
      perforated, it is too late to reverse the process.

      Perforating under-balanced is desirable since the differential pressure across the perforation
       interval (between the reservoir and the wellbore) is beneficial in cleaning the debris left in the
      perforation tunnel. Under-balanced perforating is only practiced in cases where there is no
     danger of the downhole perforating gun from being blown out of the hole. The exact method
       of perforating will be decided in due time based on optimum choice selection approach.

     The witness engineer will submit a detailed record of all perforating activities, with diagrams
     and correlation steps clearly explained. The purpose of this report is to retrace the perforating
       activities in case of doubt. The Service company perforating log, as it stands, is incomplete
     and cannot be used to recreate the perforating sequence of events. The engineer should
      prepare a Completion Report, documenting well activities, within a maximum of two weeks
       after the job

      Before running the perforation string, the firing mechanism should be chosen so that to ensure
        all the explosives have been fired properly.

     Summary of Perforation Operation sequence would be as following:

      Arm the Perforation Guns based on the desired recognized intervals

       Rig up Perforation Equipment

      RIH perforation Guns to target depth

       Perform Perforation

      Check Wellhead Pressure.

      Send perforation Job Summary to the office

    11. Waste Management Program

     Because of highland situation and space limitation of W030N location, it is not possible to rig
     up Full package of waste management equipment and system, therefore all wastes include
         drill cutting, dumped mud and surface waters will be conducted and collected in the waste pit
      during the operation. A Semi-package of Dewatering system proportionate to well location has
     been considered to recover the waste water for re-use in rig washing, cementing and drilling
      operations. Solidification of Produced Cuttings would be done according to waste management
     scope of Work. Also, in case of severe losses and need to supply excess amounts of water,
           it is planned to use extra water tanks and recovered water of dewatering system. At the end of
        drilling operation, after rig moving, the dried cutting will be transported to assigned location as
      disposal area.

      Following is a calculation table of produced cuttings and estimated total mud dump volume for
      well W030N. It should be noted that the calculations exclude any surface produced waste
      water. As the surface location of well W030N is not prepared yet, Details of waste management
     program would be provided in Waste management services’ Scope of Work.

    12.  Health, Safety and Environment

    12.1 General   Quality,   Health,   Safety  and   Environmental
        Requirements

    COMPANY is committed to conducting operations in a manner which minimizes the risks to
      the health and safety of those involved in, and affected by, such operations. COMPANY is also
     committed to conducting its operations in a manner which minimizes the impact on natural and
         ‘built’ environments in the area of operations.

           1.  This section sets out minimum Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental (QHSE)
            requirements for the WORK that CONTRACTOR and subcontractors will be required
              to comply with whilst conducting operations for COMPANY.

           2. COMPANY may perform  audits and assessments  of CONTRACTOR’s and  its
             subcontractors’ performance under the CONTRACT. COMPANY reserves the right
             without prior notice to conduct quality, health, safety, security and environmental audits
              of the Operations.

           3. CONTRACTOR shall at all times be responsible for performing the WORK in a manner
           so as to protect against loss of life, injury to people, damage to property and the
             environment. The detailed manner means and methods of performing the WORK shall
           be under the control and direction of CONTRACTOR.

           4.  Prior to the start of Operations, certain QHSE processes must be completed. These
         QHSE processes include developing the final QHSE plan format and frequency of any
         QHSE audits, permitting and licensing and COMPANY’s approvals. CONTRACTOR
               shall ensure that sufficient resources are dedicated to this task to ensure prior to
              mobilization.

           5. COMPANY may at any time stop the WORK or any portion of the WORK without
             penalty to COMPANY if the WORK is not conducted in accordance with the Quality,
             Health, Safety or Environmental guidelines specified in this CONTRACT or by the laws
              of the appropriate jurisdiction. COMPANY reserves the right to require CONTRACTOR
              to remove any person from the Operations in the case of non-compliance with QHSE
             procedures. COMPANY may also prohibit the use of equipment and plant in cases
           where that equipment or plant does not meet the required standards or is deemed
             unsafe.

           6. CONTRACTOR shall ensure that  activities associated with this CONTRACT are
            conducted in compliance with applicable national and local HSE laws and regulations,
         CONTRACTOR’s standards and COMPANY’s requirements and IADC documents.

    12.3 Environmental Management

      12.3.1 CONTRACTOR  shall comply  with any and  all  laws,  rules and  regulations  of
     governmental agencies having jurisdiction, which now exist or may be promulgated during the
      term of the CONTRACT, relating to the control and prevention of damage to the environment.

      12.3.2 Without prejudice to Item 3.1 above, CONTRACTOR shall ensure that all personnel
     use the highest prevailing standards of care and diligence to prevent unlawful disposal of all
     waste oil, water and other waste materials or fluids which may accumulate or be caused by
    CONTRACTOR’s performance of the CONTRACT. CONTRACTOR shall not dispose of any
      objects, scrap, waste, rubbish, equipment, fluids or fuel into the surrounding area or allow
      anything to be stored loose where   it can be driven  into surrounding areas by wind.
    CONTRACTOR shall take all reasonable precautions to prevent pollution of any nature or kind

    12.8 Well Control

       (1) Recording Reference

       All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud system
     and well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by
      both the Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall
      also be recorded in the Daily Drilling Report.

     Note: Flow Meter should be Used During Drilling Operation Until Rig Released.

       (2) Flow Check Procedure

     To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times
      during the drilling operation.
              •  While drilling (any warning sign)
              •   Prior to tripping the drill string
              •  While tripping (any warning sign)
              •  While out of hole(continuously)
              •   Trip out:
           ➢   After pulling 5% of the drill pipe

           ➢  At the midpoint depth of the wellbore

           ➢   Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars

           ➢   After all the drill string is out of hole.
              •   Trip in:

           ➢  Upon reaching surface casing shoe

                                                                                         Page 199 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                  Drilling Program For
                                   Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

Page 200 of 208              Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05                Rev:05

           ➢  At midpoint of the wellbore

       (3) Primary Control Reference

          It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the
      available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices
      are being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

     Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

     The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor,
       either after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

     The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke
      control panel.

     The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be
     posted on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

     The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure.
     Awareness of these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid
      formation breakdown.

     Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps
       at the following times:

               1)  Once per tour.

               2)  Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.

               3)  Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the string, BHA,
                        jet size, jet plugged or jet lost, etc.

               4)  Secondary Control Reference

            Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the
               well shall be carried out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be
           known to the Driller at all times to keep tool joints clear of annular preventer and rams.

               5)  Kick Detection Procedure While Drilling

                        If there is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the Driller shall follow the kick
               detection procedures outlined below:

             Stop drilling with the pump on→Pick up top drive to a predetermined space-out
             position→Shut off the pumps and check for well flow by visual examination on the bell
               nipple or flow line.

                     If the well is not flowing:
              •  Immediately notify the rig manager, Drilling Supervisor and Tool pusher.
              •  The Drilling Supervisor will decide whether to circulate bottoms up or resume
                       drilling. The penetration rate will be limited as long as the cause of the abnormal
                   situation is undetermined. Always be aware that some hydrocarbons (gas or oil cut
              mud) may rise to the surface. Ensure that the proper monitoring and safety
               systems all in place.

                     If the well is flowing:

                                                                                         Page 200 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                  Drilling Program For
                                   Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

Page 201 of 208              Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05                Rev:05

              •  Close the well as per the Shut-in Procedure.
              •  Immediately notify the Wellsite Drilling Supervisor, rig manager and Tool pusher.

       (4) Soft Shut-in Procedure and Line Up

      During operations the circuit has to be lined up as follows:
              •  Manuel valve on choke line is opened
              •   Hydraulic valve on choke line has to be closed
              •  The choke on choke manifold has to be opened
              •   All the valves leading to the separator passing by the choke (downstream valves)
               have to be in open positions.
              •  Beside these valves, all the valves have to be in closed position.

          Soft Shut in procedure while drilling
         The procedure is performed as follows:

                  -  if there is any kick indication, stop rotation, pick up off bottom and space out (Tool
                joint one meter above rotary table to avoid getting the next tool joint on the pipe rams)

                  - Stop pumps, perform flow check. If the well is flowing then:

                  - Open choke line valve at the BOP stack (Called HCR)

                  - Close annular BOP

                  - Close Choke

                  - Read and Record pressures and times. Check pit volume gain in order to prepare the
                     kill sheet

                  - If the gas is migrating, control the wellbore pressures during the shut in.

          Soft Shut in procedure while tripping
                      If there is any kick indication, stop tripping immediately. Here, two different
              situations can be identified:

               a) The well is flowing, then the shut in is proceeded as follows:

                    - Set the string on the slips

                    - Install a fully opening safety valve in open position. Close the valve once is installed

                    - Open choke line valve at BOP stack (HCR valve)

                    - Close annular BOP

                    - Close choke.

                    - Read and record pressures and times, check pit volumes

                        It depends on the situation to weather to start killing procedures or to strip back to the

                                                                                         Page 201 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                                  Drilling Program For
                                   Well: W030N
                            Siah Makan Oil Field

Page 202 of 208              Doc. No: SI-110-PEDC-W030-DR-DM-1097-D05                Rev:05

              bottom.

                    - If the stripping is faced, then, Stab IBOP (Grey valve)

                    - Open the fully opening safety valve

                    - Reduce the annular pressure and start stripping the string to the bottom

              b) The well is not flowing:

                    - Set the string on the slips

                    - Install IBOP (grey valve or non-return valve)

                    - Run back in the hole with controlling the volumes, if any anomalies are noticed then
             proceed to the stripping. Once on bottom, circulate annular volume and evaluate the
                 situation.

    12.9 H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure

     PEDC employs expert services of a general Contractor with specific knowledge, capability
     and resources to plan, manage and implement the H2S Safety Services for drilling wells in
      Siah Makan Oil field for duration of 24 months from starting the first well to end of Project.
     Employed Contractor must be ready to support at least two (2) wells with all equipment and
      accessories, ready and available for this project.

      The amount of Corrosive Gas has not been measured in Asmari and Pabdeh Reservoirs
     and is subjected to future samplings and well testing, but it has been supposed that H2S gas
       to be present in all Reservoir sections. For Bangestan Reservoir, the H2S content has been
      reported to be equal to 0.56 mole percent (5600 PPM).

     12.9.1 General Requirements of H2S Service

        Contractor shall provide the H2S monitoring and control services to protect against high
      concentrations of H2S gas expected through the drilling operation of Asmari & Bangestan
      Formations. Some of main responsibilities are:
      • To ensure all H2S Safety equipment is in good condition.
      • To supply, maintain, inspect, calibrate and repair all H2S equipment to the highest standard
       and have this equipment ready to use all the time.
      • To supply gas detectors & required accessories to automate the gas detection program with
          capability of continually evaluate the condition, collect information and provide automate &
       manual alerts regarding the status of the available toxic gases.
      • To review Company’s H2S evacuation procedure and to advise where change/modifications
        are required.
      • To monitor levels of H2S and other hazardous gases, inform Company, and take any
        necessary precautions to safeguard  life, the well and the Equipment from impending
        danger.

         audible alarms at different points of the rig site, to allow for early warning of all personnel
       on the rig for H2S gas occurrence in the atmosphere, hence ease of following emergency

        This system shall provide at time of gas detection and alarm for essential personnel, who
            will be responsible to control the well during emergencies, also an extended period of time
        under fresh breathing air, to allow for non-essential personnel to escape to safe briefing
         areas, and for rescue teams to rescue any injured persons during H2S emergencies.
      •  Safety supervision  shall be performed by  qualified personnel  at  rig  site,  to  install,
        commission and maintains  in good condition the H2S safety equipment, to train  rig
         personnel, Company and Third-Party personnel on H2S emergency procedures and use of
         the H2S safety equipment and to assist in carrying out the H2S Safety Plan.

     12.9.2 Monitoring H2S
      • Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker, and
           drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and alarm system
       can be used.
      • Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is 10mg/m3, unable
        warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to operators. The second warning
          level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can
         give an alarm automatically, and warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well
           site. The audible alarm should be installed on Kelly board.
      •  Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should large than
         24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators，2 sets of portable H2S
        monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person specially assigned for
         taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do periodical check to keep this
        equipment in a good condition.
      • H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

      •  After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.
      •  Contractor shall implement H2S service system by himself or 3rd party for controlling the
              risk of H2S leakage.

     12.9.3 Measures for H2S prevention
      • Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and prevailing wind
             direction of Saadat Abad oil field, off well site. In emergency, employees must follow the
           evacuation procedure.
      •  Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling fluid
           tanks to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.
      • The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate protective
           apparatus in accordance with IPS. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check
           the apparatus.
      • The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool pusher is in
          charge of the supervision and examination.
      • The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to
          measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be kept
             at less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.
      •  Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to IPS during operations in
            polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.
      • When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be
           performed due to well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to
           procedures in IPS.
      • Once blowout occurs, the incident shall be reported to the higher-level department as soon
          as possible and firefighting trucks, ambulances, medical care personnel and technicians
             shall be on duty at the well site.
      •  After the blowout is controlled, H2S concentration should be measured in the places where
        H2S is possible to gather.
      • The personnel are not allowed to access until the H2S concentration is below the critical
            concentration.

     12.9.4 H2S Monitoring & Control

     The H2S system equipment provided shall be designed for the safety-zone-area classification
     where they are deployed. Equipment supplied by the service company for the purpose of the
     work shall at all times be maintained in good conditions of the performance of the services.
     Company’s Minimum Requirements for H2S Equipment are provided in below table:
